title: Van Nuys
name: Van Nuys
metaTitle: 1031 Exchange Advisory in Van Nuys, CA
metaDescription: Van Nuys 1031 exchange advisory for owners of airport-adjacent flex buildings, production-support industrial space, and pre-1978 apartments under LA rent rules.

sections.html: Van Nuys anchors the eastern San Fernando Valley around a working general-aviation airport, a civic center that draws government-related office demand, and blocks of older apartment buildings that make up much of the Valley's rental housing stock. An owner selling in Van Nuys is usually holding one of those categories, and each one has its own quirks that a straight comparable-sales search will not surface on its own. A buyer touring more than one Van Nuys asset type in the same afternoon should resist comparing them directly, since a courthouse-adjacent office suite and an airport-adjacent flex building draw on entirely different tenant pools despite sitting only a short drive apart.

sections.heading: Airport-Adjacent Flex and Production-Support Industrial
sections.html:
Van Nuys Airport is one of the busier general-aviation fields in the country, and flex buildings nearby serve a mix of aviation-support tenants, light assembly, and small production companies drawn to the Valley's proximity to the entertainment industry. Some of that industrial stock includes soundstage or production-support space that trades on a different basis than a standard flex building, since a tenant's build-out for production use is not always easy to convert back to conventional light-industrial use.

The civic center area near the Van Nuys courthouse and government offices supports a smaller pocket of office demand tied to public-sector tenants and the attorneys and service businesses that cluster around a courthouse, which behaves differently than office demand driven by private-sector employment elsewhere in the Valley.

sections.heading: The Building Stock an Owner Is Actually Choosing Among
sections.html:
Given how varied Van Nuys real estate is block to block, a replacement search assembled for a Van Nuys property typically draws from:

  • Airport-adjacent flex and light-industrial buildings
  • Production-support and soundstage-adjacent industrial space
  • Pre-1978 garden apartment buildings along Van Nuys Boulevard and nearby corridors
  • Small office space near the civic center and courthouse
  • DST interests for owners exiting active property management

sections.heading: Rent Stabilization on Van Nuys's Older Apartment Stock
sections.html:
Much of Van Nuys's multifamily stock was built in the 1960s and 1970s, which puts it under the city of Los Angeles's own rent stabilization ordinance in addition to whatever exemption or coverage applies under the statewide AB 1482 cap. A lender underwriting one of these buildings will want the rent roll checked against the local ordinance specifically, since it can be more restrictive than the statewide cap depending on the unit's history and any prior vacancy decontrol.

A buyer looking at production-support industrial space should also confirm the tenant's build-out does not create a use restriction that would complicate re-leasing to a conventional industrial tenant, since specialized soundstage improvements are not always an asset from a re-leasing standpoint.

sections.heading: Matching Identification Strategy to the Right Category
sections.html: An owner exchanging out of a pre-1978 Van Nuys apartment building can often stay within the three-property rule if the search stays inside comparable Valley multifamily. Someone exiting airport-adjacent flex or production-support industrial and open to a broader mix typically needs the 200 percent rule, since those categories underwrite differently enough that a narrow three-property list rarely covers the right range before the forty-five day deadline.

sections.heading: Line-Item Budgeting for a Van Nuys Replacement Purchase
sections.html:
A numbers-first budget for a pre-1978 Van Nuys apartment building should carry an explicit reserve for deferred maintenance typical of 1960s and 1970s garden-style construction, including plumbing and electrical systems original to the building, rather than relying on a general capital reserve percentage pulled from a newer-vintage comparable. Rent-roll underwriting should also model the local rent stabilization ordinance's allowable annual increase rather than a market-rate growth assumption, since the two produce very different cash flow projections.

Lifecycle cost on production-support industrial space should include a line for de-specializing the building if the current soundstage-style improvements would limit the pool of future industrial tenants, since a buyer planning to re-lease to a conventional light-industrial user may need to budget for removing or converting those improvements. Getting a contractor's estimate on that conversion cost before closing, rather than after signing a new tenant, avoids an unpleasant surprise in the first year of ownership. A buyer should treat that conversion estimate as a real offset to purchase price rather than a post-closing surprise, since it can meaningfully change the effective basis of the replacement property.

faqs.q: Does production-support industrial space in Van Nuys re-lease as easily as standard flex space?
faqs.a: Not always. Specialized soundstage or production build-outs can create use restrictions that complicate re-leasing to a conventional industrial tenant, so a buyer should factor that into the underwriting rather than treat the space as generic flex.

faqs.q: How does Los Angeles's rent stabilization ordinance affect a Van Nuys apartment purchase?
faqs.a: Buildings from the 1960s and 1970s common in Van Nuys typically fall under the city's own rent stabilization ordinance, which can be more restrictive than the statewide AB 1482 cap depending on vacancy history. A lender will want the rent roll checked against the local ordinance specifically.

faqs.q: Why does office demand near the Van Nuys courthouse behave differently than elsewhere in the Valley?
faqs.a: It is driven largely by public-sector tenants and the attorneys and service businesses that cluster around a courthouse, which follows a different pattern than office demand tied to private-sector employment in the rest of the Valley.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Los Angeles confirm my Van Nuys property qualifies for an exchange?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates planning, property identification, and communication among an investor's advisors. Whether a specific transaction and property qualify is a determination made by the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.
